name: Aloo Bharta (Potato Mash)

ingredients.name: Dry red chilli (shukno lonka) or green chilli

steps.text: Wash and boil the potatoes until fork-tender, then drain, cool slightly, and peel off the skins.
Heat mustard oil until smoking, fry dry red chillies until crisp, and crush them with a pinch of salt. Optionally lightly sauté half of the chopped onion.
Mash the warm potatoes smoothly with crushed chillies, raw or fried onion, green chilli, fresh coriander leaves, salt, and raw mustard oil. Serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Using pungent kachi ghani mustard oil and a mix of raw and lightly fried onions gives authentic Bengali Aloo Bharta flavour.

name: Aloo Chokha (Bihari Spiced Potato Bharta)

ingredients.name: Green chillies & roasted dry red chilli

steps.text: Boil potatoes until soft, peel, and mash while warm so no large lumps remain.
Roast dry red chillies and garlic cloves over a direct flame or in a dry pan until aromatic, then crush coarsely.
Fold finely chopped onion, crushed garlic-chilli, green chillies, coriander, lemon juice, salt, and raw mustard oil into the mashed potatoes.

notes: Pairs classically with dal-chawal, khichdi, or litti.

name: Begun Bharta (Roasted Eggplant Mash)

steps.text: Wash the brinjal, make 2–3 slits to check for blemishes, optionally tuck garlic cloves and a green chilli inside, and rub the skin lightly with oil.
Roast directly over an open gas flame, turning frequently until the skin is completely charred and the flesh collapses softly.
Cool slightly, peel off the charred skin, and mash the smoky flesh with raw chopped onion, green chillies, fresh coriander, salt, and pungent mustard oil.

notes: In Bengal this raw-onion mustard-oil mash is called Begun Pora / Begun Bharta and pairs wonderfully with hot roti or winter khichuri.

name: Bhindi Bharta (Okra / Dherosh Mash)

ingredients.name: Dry red chilli or green chilli

steps.text: Wash tender okra pods, trim only the tips after steaming, and steam over boiling water (or char on a dry tawa) for 7–8 minutes until tender.
Fry dry red chillies in mustard oil until crisp, then crush with salt and chopped onion.
Trim stems from the cooked okra and mash gently with the onion-chilli mixture, mustard oil, and optional lemon juice.

notes: Steaming whole okra before trimming the caps prevents excessive mucilage (stickiness).

Heat mustard oil in a pan and fry or steam-fry the karela slices with garlic on medium-low heat until tender and lightly browned.
Coarsely mash or pound the cooked karela with finely chopped onion, crushed chilli, salt, and a drizzle of raw mustard oil.

notes: Salting and resting karela before cooking mellows the bitterness while keeping its digestive benefits.

name: Kochur Mukhi Bharta (Taro Root / Arbi Mash)

ingredients.name: Kochur Mukhi / Gathi Kochu / Arbi (Taro root)

steps.text: Wash taro roots and boil or pressure-cook with skins on until soft, then cool slightly and slip off the skins.
Mash the peeled taro roots smoothly with chopped onion, crushed roasted garlic and chillies, lemon juice, salt, and mustard oil.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve warm with steamed rice and dal.

notes: Creamy texture that pairs wonderfully with plain masoor or moong dal.

name: Lau Bharta (Bottle Gourd Mash)

steps.text: Peel the bottle gourd, remove any large seeds, and grate or chop finely.
Simmer the bottle gourd covered in its own juices with a pinch of salt until soft, then uncover and cook until excess water evaporates.
Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds, garlic, onion, and green chillies, add the cooked gourd, and mash on the pan until cohesive. Garnish with coriander.

notes: Light, cooling, and easy to digest.

name: Patol Bharta (Pointed Gourd / Parwal Mash)

steps.text: Wash and scrape patol (pointed gourd). Either char whole over an open flame or boil halved patol until soft, removing any tough mature seeds.
Coarsely mash or grind the cooked patol with garlic and green chillies.

Heat mustard oil, temper with nigella seeds and dry red chilli, sauté chopped onion until translucent, and stir in the patol mash until moisture evaporates. Finish with coriander and a drop of raw mustard oil.

notes: Also known as Potol Bharta in West Bengal and Parwal Chokha in Bihar and eastern UP.

name: Sajne Data Bharta (Drumstick / Moringa Pod Pulp Mash)

steps.text: Cut drumsticks into 3-inch pieces and boil in salted water until soft.
Split the boiled drumsticks and scrape out the soft inner pulp and tender seeds with a spoon, discarding the woody outer fibres.
Mash the drumstick pulp with mustard paste, finely chopped onion, crushed green chillies, salt, and raw mustard oil.

notes: Nutrient-dense seasonal spring bharta popular in Bengal.

name: Shim Bharta (Flat Beans Mash)

Fold in finely chopped raw onion, fresh coriander leaves, and a drizzle of mustard oil.

notes: A beloved winter Bengali delicacy.

Mash warm ucche and potato together with chopped green chillies, salt, and raw mustard oil. Serve as a traditional Bengali first-course starter with hot rice.

notes: Traditionally eaten at the start of a Bengali lunch with hot steamed rice (gorom bhaat).

name: Ukadiche Modak

steps.text: Measure ingredients. Soak, grate, grind or knead the ingredients as needed for the sweet; prepare any filling before cooking.
Cook the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring regularly to prevent sticking. For fried sweets, shape carefully and cook until done before soaking in syrup if applicable.
Add the listed flavourings and garnish. Cool or chill until set when required, then serve.

notes: This is a starter recipe outline; traditional sweets vary by region. Adjust proportions and method to the preferred household style.
